title: Part 107 in High School CTE: How Schools Run It
sub_heading: How schools run FAA Part 107 prep as a semester or full-year CTE course, and what teachers see on the manager dashboard.
body_html:
In short: A strong high school drone program pairs structured Part 107 knowledge test prep with a delivery model your staff can actually run—teacher-led, hybrid, or self-paced—and gives program leads visibility into student progress without chasing spreadsheets. Drone Edge is browser-based: units, sections, practice questions, and exams, plus an org manager dashboard for cohort progress and scores.

FAA Part 107 is live today. A Drone Building course (design, 3D-print, and fly) opens in early access in January 2027. This article covers how Part 107 fits CTE schedules, what students and teachers experience, and when a consultation makes sense.

Key takeaways

  • Part 107 fits CTE when framed as industry credential prep plus safe operations—not a one-off club activity.
  • Delivery is flexible: daily bell schedule, block rotation, hybrid homework, or fully async for workforce learners.
  • Students move through structured units with section practice and unit exams; progress saves to each student's account.
  • Teachers and program leads use the manager dashboard to see roster activity, unit completion, and exam scores.
  • Hardware is separate: flight labs and kits are optional complements; knowledge test prep is software.

Where Part 107 sits in a CTE pathway

Career and technical education buyers usually want three things: a credential employers recognize, skills students can demonstrate, and documentation for accreditors and grants offices. FAA Part 107—the remote pilot certificate for commercial small UAS operations—checks the credential box for many pathways (aviation, public safety, media production, inspection-adjacent careers).

Drone Edge maps content to ACS-style domains in nested units and sections, with practice items and exams at unit and course level. That structure helps curriculum committees see pacing and outcomes instead of a folder of videos.

Typical program homes include career academies, aviation or engineering CTE, STEM electives, workforce continuing education, and after-school clubs that feed into a formal course. If your program already owns drones, think of Part 107 prep as the knowledge and compliance layer alongside optional flight lab time.

Delivery models that work in schools

Teacher-led classroom

The instructor sets weekly unit targets; students work through sections in class. Unit exams can be assigned as milestones. Homework extends reading and practice questions. Best when you have a dedicated drone or aviation teacher and stable lab or computer access.

Hybrid

Async section work at home; class time for discussion, remediation, and optional flight activities. Fits block schedules and shared CTE labs where seat time is limited.

Self-paced / workforce

Community college or adult workforce cohorts progress individually; the manager dashboard still shows who is stuck before the testing center date. Useful for short bootcamp-style offerings.

All models are browser-based—no app install. BYOD is supported; schools set their own device policies.

What students see

After joining an org (invite code or roster process your admin configures), students open the Part 107 course and see a clear unit outline. Each unit contains sections with text, media, and inline practice. Section-level checks build toward unit exams; the course includes full practice exams for knowledge test preparation.

Progress persists per student: completed sections, exam attempts, and scores. Students always know what is next; teachers are not the bottleneck for "what page are we on?"

Individuals can preview Unit 1 free on the public course preview; school orgs access the full course under your program agreement.

What teachers and program leads see

The manager dashboard is where most school evaluations are won or lost. Program leads and assigned managers log in to an org-scoped view:

  • Classes and periods — group students by period (for example "Period 2" and "Period 5") and filter every view by class
  • Progress — a lesson grid by student, with videos watched, time in the last 7 days, last active date, and an effort signal
  • Quizzes and exams — each student's first, best, and latest scores, number of tries, and weak sections, so you can tell "still trying" from "stuck"
  • Class exams — generate an exam for a class and see results for that roster
  • CSV export — for grade books, board reports, and grant evidence

That visibility supports weekly check-ins, early intervention, and grant or board reporting without exporting from a consumer app. It is the difference between "we bought content" and "we run a program with accountability."

Org accounts support multiple manager seats (teacher plus CTE director, for example). Student accounts are separate from managers; roles are enforced in the product.

What is live vs roadmap

Live: the FAA Part 107 structured course with more than 450 practice questions tagged to the FAA's test standards, org accounts with classes and invite codes, the manager dashboard, and browser delivery.

Questions answered

Do we need drones in the building to use this?

No for knowledge test prep. Many programs add flight labs separately. Drone Edge covers structured Part 107 content and exams; hardware is your choice.

How many students can we run?

School packages start at $79 per seat and are quoted by seat count and term (pilot semester or full year). Book a consultation with your expected headcount.

Does this integrate with our LMS?

Browser-based delivery today. SSO, Google Classroom, and LTI are roadmap items—ask what integration is a blocker vs nice-to-have for your district.

Can you guarantee students pass the FAA test?

No. We provide honest prep depth and practice density; we do not publish pass rates. Many schools start with a pilot semester to evaluate fit.

How does this relate to funding?

Drone programs often map to CTE, STEM, and workforce language. See our funding considerations page and our guide to funding a school drone program in 2026—eligibility is always district- and grant-specific.
